text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.08% today after oil prices stabilized following earlier geopolitical uncertainty. Over the past few days, crude fell sharply on August 25th when the market feared military escalation with Iran, but recovered when it became clear the U.S. is pursuing economic pressure rather than direct military action — and as Iran and Oman began negotiating a deal to keep the crucial Strait of Hormuz open for shipping. That de-escalation lifted crude back up, which benefits refiners like Marathon by improving margins on fuel production.

The stock's bounce today also reflects a broader two-week gain (up 4% since mid-August) as energy markets have priced in reduced geopolitical risk to Middle Eastern oil supplies. A refiner's profitability depends heavily on the spread between crude oil input costs and refined product prices — when supply disruption fears fade, that spread typically improves and shares recover.
